subject: Dedicated pool preemption & latency exception request — Windfall AI
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@windfall.ai>, procurement@windfall.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool preemption & latency exception request — Windfall AI

Hi Ellen / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the time earlier. As discussed, Windfall is evaluating a 4-GPU dedicated pool for inference of your dialog agent. Before we move to a formal SOW, your team asked for a written exception request around preemption and queueing behavior during higher-than-expected traffic and routine maintenance windows.

Summary of ask (high level):
- No preemption of the dedicated pool for scheduled maintenance during business hours (08:00-20:00 PT) OR an equivalent hard SLA that ensures workload continuity.
- p95 latency guarantee for single-turn generative calls (prompt + <=256 tokens) under normal operational concurrency: target p95 <= 250 ms.
- Throughput commitment: baseline 350k generated tokens / minute sustained across the 4-GPU pool (approx 87.5k tokens/min per GPU).
- Queue behavior: when contention occurs, Windfall requests that requests queue rather than be preempted or routed to lower-tier shared capacity unless queue wait > 2s, in which case automatic fallback may be allowed.

Can you confirm these are the constraints you want captured? If so, we will draft a targeted SLA addendum and propose mitigations (headroom reservation, controlled draining, warm standby in a secondary AZ) and commercial terms.

We expect to attach a short capacity workbook and a draft redline to the SOW — I'll send both in the follow-up.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: none in this initial note

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@windfall.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@windfall.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool preemption & latency exception request — Windfall AI

Jordan,

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifying questions from our side before Procurement/Legal will sign off on an exception:

1) Traffic profile — peak concurrency (RPS) and distribution across the day. We need a 72-hr sample or an expected QPS curve so our SREs can model KV-cache warmups.
2) What is your tolerable monthly preemption budget, if any? Windfall cannot tolerate >5% minutes lost during business hours; if Redwood needs a maintenance window we need either no preemption or an automated capacity-failover to a hot standby.
3) Fallback behavior — if Redwood chooses to route to shared hosted capacity, will the model variant be identical (same weights/quantization) and will context tokens be preserved? Not acceptable if model variant materially degrades quality.

Also, can you confirm whether the latency target is for token-emission latency or end-to-end response (including batching and tokenization)? We prefer end-to-end.

If you can send the sample traffic and a proposed draft addendum we can move faster. Procurement would like to see uplift pricing tied to the no-preempt option and any headroom reservation.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Windfall AI

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@windfall.ai>, procurement@windfall.ai

Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool preemption & latency exception request — Windfall AI

Ellen — thanks, great questions. Answers below and attaching the capacity workbook + draft redline for SOW.

1) Traffic profile: see attached workbook (windfall-capacity-calcs.xlsx). Short summary:
   - Typical weekday peak: 180 concurrent request slots (~30 RPS sustained during spike windows).
   - Average daily queries: ~1.2M requests/day, with bursts up to 3x baseline for up to 45 minutes.

2) Preemption budget: we can work with you on a hard cap. Proposal: allow up to 2% preemption minutes per calendar month for emergency maintenance only. For planned maintenance during business hours we propose a rolling drain window with live handoff to warm standby; preference is no in-window preemption.

3) Fallback behavior: if we must route off-pool, we guarantee a model-compatible fallback (same architecture, matched quantization profile and prompt templates). We will also support a KV-prefill strategy (prefix caching) so context preservation is best-effort but we will target >90% match-rate for common prompts. We will not route to a lower-quality variant without prior consent.

Latency definition: we propose end-to-end (request received -> final token emitted). The 250 ms p95 target is for typical prompt+<=256-token generation; if your distribution skews longer we can add a tiered p95 (e.g., <=256 tokens p95: 250 ms; <=1024 tokens p95: 600 ms).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sla-redlines.pdf, windfall-capacity-calcs.xlsx

Please review — we can incorporate Procurement's uplift % request into the commercial sheet.

Best,
Jordan

Subject: RE: Dedicated pool preemption & latency exception request — Windfall AI

Ellen / Jordan — quick technical note from infra / runtime side to set expectations:

- Warm standby: we can provision a hot standby pool in the same region (cross-AZ) that keeps KV caches warm by replaying a sampled prefix stream. Warm standby reduces failover latency to <30s for routing but requires ~15% additional reserved headroom on GPUs.

- Draining / preemption: graceful node drain (stop accepting new steady-state requests, finish in-flight tokens, migrate sessions) is feasible but KV reconstruction on a new node can take up to 2-3 minutes depending on cache size and prompt variety; that feeds into our suggestion to keep queued requests rather than force immediate routing.

- Headroom & batching: to hit the 250 ms p95 target we recommend reserving 12-18% headroom for spikes and tuning batching windows to 8-12 ms. If Windfall can accept a short, bounded queue (<=2s), we can preserve p95 without larger reserve.

- Metrics to include in the SLA addendum: p95 end-to-end latency, queue wait distribution (p50/p95), monthly availability (99.95% target), and preemption minutes budget.

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through tradeoffs.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@windfall.ai>, procurement@windfall.ai, legal@windfall.ai
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 3 Jul 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated pool preemption & latency exception request — Windfall AI

Ellen / Procurement / Legal — thanks for moving quickly on this. Based on Jordan + Karthik's notes, Redwood can offer a controlled "no-preempt" addendum under these conditions:

1) Minimum term: 12 months committed for the 4-GPU pool.
2) Pricing uplift: 25% premium over standard Dedicated SKU to cover reserved headroom and warm standby costs. We can present a 9-12 month stepdown if Windfall increases commit after 6 months.
3) SLA language preview:
   - Monthly availability (pool-level): 99.95%
   - p95 end-to-end latency for prompt+<=256 tokens: <=250 ms (measured at our ingress layer)
   - Queue behavior: requests will queue up to 2s before allowed automatic fallback; queueing beyond 2s triggers routing to backup pool only with notification and an agreed fallback model variant.
   - Preemption budget: <=2% minutes per calendar month for emergency maintenance only; planned maintenance subject to 72-hr notice and preferred after-hours scheduling.

4) Next steps: Legal can redline the attached PDF (redwood-dedicated-sla-redlines.pdf). Procurement — please confirm whether the uplift is acceptable and if Windfall requires additional audit obligations (SOC3, extended logging retention).

If Procurement agrees, Jordan will circulate an updated SOW and we will lock pricing for the term.

Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
